correctness.rationale: Source RESULT.md explicitly gives bias-corrected silent-history moment factors c1=(1-beta1)/(1-beta1^tau) and c2=sqrt((1-beta2)/(1-beta2^tau)). Hence mini coordinate update denominator is c2||g||_2/sqrt(d)+epsilon versus c2|g_j|+epsilon for Adam. Cancelling the identical numerator yields the claimed ratio. |g_j|<=||g|| proves <=sqrt(d), achieved in the infinite-impulse-amplitude limit for one nonzero coordinate with fixed epsilon>0. Equal k-support gives sqrt(d/k). Maximizing over blocks produces sqrt(max d_b) and pigeonhole gives the optimal sqrt(ceil(N/B)); balanced partitions attain it. Independent new checks covered d<=14, all k, and small integer partitions. No claim of actual training-loss amplification is proven.
residual_risks: Requires the specified scalar mean-square blocks and same epsilon placement, zero initial moments, no decay; blocks treated coordinatewise by Adam-mini are excluded.
Positive epsilon gives a limiting supremum, not finite-amplitude attainment.

value.rationale: The scalar-memory compression in Adam-mini creates a mathematically meaningful, optimizer-specific sparse-coordinate response vulnerability. The sharp sqrt(d/k) support law and sqrt(ceil(N/B)) memory-count frontier quantify the exact unavoidable cost, which a researcher can use when choosing or testing partitions under sparse updates. This is not asserted as a universal training-loss or convergence guarantee; its elementary pigeonhole step is only part of the calculation, not the significance by itself.
residual_risks: Balanced partitions may be bad for Hessian geometry; the value lies only in isolated-impulse robustness.

final_claim: For scalar-mean-square Adam-mini blocks with zero pre-impulse gradients and matching Adam hyperparameters, the active-coordinate impulse amplification is at most sqrt(d), sharp on a large-amplitude one-coordinate impulse; for k equal-magnitude active coordinates it tends to sqrt(d/k); N coordinates grouped into B nonempty blocks have sharp minimax worst gain sqrt(ceil(N/B)).
limitations: Only blocks using scalar averaged-square state, not architecture-specific coordinatewise exceptions.
Silent gradient history, epsilon>0, beta1,beta2 in [0,1), no weight decay.
Sharp factors are high-impulse suprema, not loss bounds or global optimizer quality statements.
